messages:
Adam (eng-platform): Quick sync — we need to standardize how routing fallbacks surface to clients. Currently some fallbacks return 503 + body, others 200 with a model header, and a few emit 429. SDKs are handling each case differently and it's causing retries or silent failures.

Jordan (eng-runtime): We should have one contract. My vote: 429 for client throttles (quota/pacing), 503 for server-side capacity errors where no fallback is possible, and 200 when a graceful fallback model is used.

Anya (devex): +1 on separation, but 503 implies a transient server error — clients may back off even when we actually served a cheaper variant. We should provide machine-readable hints so SDKs can choose behavior.

Liz (product): Proposal: always include an error_code in JSON bodies for non-200s (e.g., "error_code":"rate_limit" or "error_code":"capacity_exhausted"). For 200-with-fallback, include a header and a small body field like "fallback_info". Keep customer-facing copy short.

Rico (eng-infra): Prefer headers for streaming use-cases. We already send X-Redwood-Model and X-Redwood-Model-Variant. Add X-Redwood-Fallback-Type: soft|hard and X-Redwood-Retryable: true|false. That keeps SDK parsing cheap.

Adam (eng-platform): Sketch of rule set: 
1) Request succeeded but used a lower-fidelity model -> 200 + X-Redwood-Fallback-Type=soft + body may include fallback_info.
2) Request failed due to capacity and no fallback available -> 503 + standardized JSON: {"error":"service_unavailable","error_code":"capacity_exhausted","retry_after":30}.
3) Client exceeded quota/pacing -> 429 + Retry-After header + error_code="rate_limit".

Jordan (eng-runtime): Edge case: pinned models. If user pins model vX but we route to a compatible quantized variant, that should be 200 w/ explicit hint (compat fallback). If fidelity changes materially, consider 503? Not ideal.

Anya (devex): Agree on 200 for compat fallback. Telemetry wise: tag these with event=route_fallback, fallback_reason and fallback_variant. Console needs a per-route %fallback metric and an alert when it exceeds threshold.

Liz (product): Console UX ideas: "fallback heatmap" per model/region, recent requests sample. Must not expose raw prompts — use hashed previews or token counts. Provide a toggle to show or hide request samples.

sre-bot: INC-382: 2026-02-03T14:12Z capacity surge -> 503 spike x3, autoscaler adjustments mitigated the issue. Linked logs in incident timeline.

Rico (eng-infra): Implementation notes: runtime will emit metric labels: fallback_type, fallback_variant, is_retryable. Need an ingestion change so traces include these labels and we can attach them to spans. Also propose a new enum for fallback_type in our proto.

Adam (eng-platform): SDK changes: release patch that interprets the new headers and maps to retry/backoff logic. Devex to provide migration guide and example code.

Liz (product): Draft of client-facing copy for 200-with-fallback: "Served from an alternative model due to capacity constraints. Responses may differ slightly." Short and neutral.

Jordan (eng-runtime): Streaming edge: if we switch model mid-stream due to a hot reroute, how do we surface that to clients? Sending 503 mid-stream is impossible.

Anya (devex): Mid-stream switches are messy for clients. Option A: runtime decides pre-stream whether fallback will happen and include header. Option B: if mid-stream switch unavoidable, emit a final metadata chunk like {"_redwood":"fallback","type":"hard"} so client can log it. But that may break some frame parsers.

Rico (eng-infra): Alternative: disallow mid-stream model switches unless both models are fully compatible. If switch happens, mark span with final_fallback and let client-side SDK reconcile on end-of-stream.

Liz (product): Rollout plan: canary (5% traffic) with console flag 'show-fallbacks-in-console' for internal users. Add admin override to force a 200-with-hint behavior for legacy integrations (but we should warn in console).

Adam (eng-platform): Action items:
- eng-runtime (Jordan + Rico): add headers and metric labels.
- eng-platform (me + Jordan): write API contract doc & example payloads.
- devex (Anya): SDK handling + migration guide and example snippets.
- product/console (Liz): fallback heatmap UI mock and copy.
I'll own the rollout schedule. Target: 2-week canary then phased ramp.

Rachel (legal): Quick note — ensure fallback labels and any samples don't leak PII. Legal wants a short checklist for console samples.

Liz (product): Noted. We'll sanitize and hash sensitive fields.

Adam (eng-platform): OK sync tomorrow 10:00am. Thanks everyone.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: platform/fallback-standardization v1 -> canary (5%).

Jordan (eng-runtime): :thumbsup: 

Anya (devex): :raised_hands:
